criteria.description: Correctly restates V* as the best achievable return maximized over first action and all decisions.
Correctly identifies Q*(s,a) as the same quantity with the first action fixed, so maxing over a recovers V*.

solutions.fullSolution: V*(s) is the best achievable expected return, maximized over every possible first action (and all subsequent decisions). Q*(s,a) is by definition the best achievable return given the first action is fixed to a, with optimal behavior thereafter. Maximizing Q*(s,a) over a therefore recovers the same maximization V*(s) already performs over its first action: V*(s)=max_a Q*(s,a).

solutions.fullSolution: Q_{k+1}(s,a) = R(s,a)+gamma*sum_s' P(s'|s,a)*max_a' Q_k(s',a') >= R(s,a)+gamma*sum_s' P(s'|s,a)*max_a'[Q*(s',a')-Delta_k]. Since sum_s' P(s'|s,a)=1, -Delta_k factors out: = [R(s,a)+gamma*sum_s' P(s'|s,a)*max_a' Q*(s',a')] - gamma*Delta_k = Q*(s,a) - gamma*Delta_k.
